info.title: Mnemic HTTP API
info.description: HTTP contract for implemented health, static documentation, configuration, project memory/conversations, JSON/SSE chat and cancellation, Provider, recall/diagnostics, PENDING, usage/export, approval and audit APIs (Issue #24). Instances without required database or master key expose a subset. Runtime refinements and operation side effects also apply; schema validation is not an authorization or readiness guarantee. Future MCP APIs are not implemented here. Error type URIs are stable identifiers, not guaranteed live web pages.

post.summary: Prepare a bounded lossless whole-instance core-table JSONL archive
post.description: Requires DB and global operator Bearer, not master key or per-project membership. Explicit scope=instance acknowledges ALL projects, conversations/messages, observations, beliefs, ALL belief_versions, memory_embeddings and raw audit_log, including sensitive/unknown historical JSONB. No project/table/query filter; unknown body and query fields rejected. Never contains provider_configs or later module tables; not a whole-database backup. One repeatable-read transaction reads rows in fixed table and UUID order in pages of8; deleted/retracted facts and inherited reference metadata remain unchanged. to_jsonb(row)::text is stored as row_json STRING to preserve numeric lexemes and microsecond timestamps; clients must not parse/reserialize through lossy JS numbers. UTF8 LF JSONL manifest/row/end format v1, trailing LF required, eight table counts and SHA256 over manifest+row bytes including LF, excluding end. Hash detects corruption, not authenticity/encryption. Fixed bounds10000rows,1MiB per encoded line,16MiB entire archive including footer; any overflow rejects the whole export, never truncates. Oversized raw rows suppressed by SQL before transfer; SQL pages<=8 rows; each query5s and lock wait1s. No hard whole-process memory/CPU guarantee. Archive is fully encoded before audit_log actor=server/action=memory.export/target=export_id/decision=prepared with counts/bytes/hash only, in same transaction. Transaction commit must succeed before any download bytes/attachment header. Current receipt is excluded from its own earlier snapshot, previous audit rows are included. prepared proves payload preparation and audit commit, NOT client delivery or disk persistence; lost responses may still leave receipts and manual retry creates another export. No importer, file write, model call, data mutation except audit. No redaction/encryption: protect transport and downloaded file. GET is not an export route. Handler hook sets no-store after root auth/rate; earlier transport errors keep existing rules. Ordinary configured CORS applies.

post.summary: Explicitly probe three model slots; may incur provider charges
post.description: CLI-only explicit action. Rejects every Origin before parsing JSON. Requires JSON empty object; unknown body keys rejected, query keys ignored. With healthy database/dimensions/config, invokes two text slots and one embedding slot concurrently, each maxRetries=0 and 15-second abort signal. Embedding length/finiteness validated. Missing config, upstream failures or model quota denial are caught into HTTP200 probe=true/ok=false reports, not guaranteed HTTP429. Report does not include generated text, keys or raw exceptions. No Evidence/Belief/retrieval trace; invocations may create usage records and consume daily quota. No automatic resend after uncertain response; abort does not prove billing stopped. The abort budget is not an end-to-end database deadline.

get.summary: Aggregate recorded project model usage without invoking models
get.description: Strict query: unknown fields and duplicate scalar fields rejected. Project/conversation UUIDs normalized to lowercase. ISO offset times require UTC years 0001-9999 and at most millisecond filter precision; runtime refinements enforce a positive window of at most 366 days. Defaults: to=server now, from=to minus 30 days. Half-open [from,to), UTC day grouping. Not all date refinements or cross-field limits are expressed by OpenAPI. Requires database, not master key. Global operator authorization, not project membership. Optional conversation_id means physical owning conversation; inherited continuation history is not recounted. Null-project probes excluded. No Provider resolution or model invocation; reads existing usage only. Provider/model labels are stored metadata, not guaranteed secret-redacted. Token totals and duration_ms are exact decimal strings; call and missing-call counts are bounded integers. Missing token coverage is not zero. Configured estimates use current pricing revision and historical effective rates; not provider bills or proof of billing stopped. Handler responses no-store; earlier auth/transport errors follow their own rules. group_by defaults to day (also model, purpose, conversation). group_limit defaults to 200, max 1000; groups_truncated refers only to group details, totals remain complete in one SQL snapshot. Missing prices yield currency/pricing_revision/known_amount=null; a zero known subtotal does not prove free usage. Reading a report does not write an export audit.

200.description: Exact recorded counts, missing coverage and optional estimates, grouped within the requested scope.

Handler responses no-store; earlier auth/transport errors follow their own rules. format query selects json (default) or csv, not the Accept header. limit defaults to 200, max 1000. after is an existing usage row UUID in the same project/conversation/window, otherwise 404. Keyset order (started_at,id) preserves PostgreSQL microseconds; reuse the returned exact from/to for subsequent pages, including when defaults were used. Each request is a separate DB transaction, not a frozen multi-page export snapshot. JSON returns records and next_after (null at end); CSV quotes all cells, doubles quotes, uses CRLF, prefixes potential spreadsheet formulas with an apostrophe and leaves null cells empty. CSV is an attachment, not JSON; it lacks a JSON envelope. X-Usage-From/To carry resolved bounds, optional X-Next-After is absent on the final page. Prepare the complete page and commit a minimal usage.export/prepared audit before sending; prepared does not mean delivered or saved by client. Audit failure returns fixed 500 with no export payload or committed receipt; lost response does not prove audit absent. Each successful page, including empty pages, writes a receipt; no automatic retry. Estimates have 12 fractional digits and exact token strings may exceed JavaScript safe integer precision.

post.summary: Persist a client-reported approval decision and return an audit receipt
post.description: Requires database, not master key. Global operator Bearer, not per-user membership authorization. URL project must exist. UUID inputs normalize to lowercase. No Provider resolution, model invocation, permission mutation or tool execution. Client-reported decisions are not server authorization or evidence of execution. Ordinary configured CORS applies; not a CLI-only Origin rejection. Handler responses no-store, earlier auth/transport errors follow their own rules. Strict JSON event body: unknown/plaintext command/path fields rejected. Body project_id must match URL project or 404 before insert. Query fields ignored. event.request_id is a client correlation UUID, independent of the HTTP x-request-id. Root/target/command SHA256 hashes are supplied by client; server cannot verify local filesystem or whether an operation ran. Allow/deny reason, operation, mode, scope, target_basis and command_hash combinations are runtime refinements, not fully encoded in OpenAPI. Null operation is allowed for denied invalid requests; shell requires command_hash and non-shell forbids it. Writes audit_log actor=cli, version=1/client_reported=true, action=approval.<operation or invalid>, target=sha256:<target_hash> or null, decision=allow/deny. First event_id insert returns201. Same normalized event under same ID returns200 with original recorded_at, without new row; different event or incompatible/colliding platform history returns409 without overwriting. Global event-ID collision does not reveal the existing payload. A lost response may follow a committed insert: if deliberately retrying the audit receipt, retain the identical event_id and payload, never regenerate it or repeat the underlying tool operation. No additional execution, rollback or cross-service exactly-once guarantee.

get.summary: Read safe projections of global operator audit history
get.description: Requires DB, not master key; route absent without DB. Global Bearer operator authorization, not per-project membership. Strict query, unknown/duplicate scalar fields rejected. UUID filters normalize lowercase; actor/action/target are allowlisted forms. project_id only compares meta.project_id as a string; it does not check project existence or include global events without that metadata (such as Provider/flags events). This is a filter, never an access boundary. Defaults: to=server now, from=to minus30 days; half-open [from,to), positive span at most366 days. Filter dates require UTC years0001-9999 and at most millisecond precision; those refinements are runtime checks. limit default50, 1..200; digit strings accepted, fractions/exponents/blanks rejected. Keyset order (ts,id), cursor must exist inside the same filters/window or404. Cursor timestamp read as PG raw text preserves microseconds; output ts also has microseconds. Reuse resolved from/to across pages; each page is a separate query, not a frozen snapshot. Unknown/corrupt/oversized (>65536 UTF8 bytes of meta::text) or envelope-inconsistent rows remain opaque history positions: id/ts retained, actor/action/target/decision/meta all null, metadata_omitted=true. Actor/action/decision >64 bytes or target >128 bytes are similarly suppressed before projection. Opaque rows still count toward limit and can serve as cursors. Known metadata is projected through existing strict schemas: platform events, gate redaction summaries and client-reported approval events. Cross-field consistency uses runtime projection and is not fully encoded by OpenAPI. This differs from the project approval endpoint, which fails the whole page for selected incompatible rows. No new audit write, permission mutation, Provider resolution or model invocation. Client reports and prepared receipts are not execution/delivery proof. Route hook sets no-store after root auth/rate admission; earlier errors obey their own rules. Ordinary CORS applies. Not a backup or proof that all real-world actions were recorded.

post.summary: Admit user/file Evidence and save a complete JSON answer
post.description: Requires database, master key and global operator Bearer; absent dependencies mean route404. UUID paths normalized to lowercase, both project and conversation must match before busy state or admission. Query ignored, strict body. text is 1–8000 characters, not trimmed. Attachments are client-declared relative paths and UTF8 text, never server file reads. Runtime refinements reject sensitive/escaping paths, duplicate paths, invalid Unicode/control bytes, more than8 files or8 directories, more than16 total entries, single content above16KiB or total above64KiB. Generated structure does not fully encode these refinements. User text is stored as supplied; only file path/content is sanitized before storage/prompt. Never submit credentials in user text. File Evidence is separately anchored to the physical user message and assigned PROJECT_FILE authority by trusted writeback, not by model/client labels. Sanitization is not complete secret detection or prompt-injection prevention. Evidence admission plus durable outbox is atomic; inherited history is validated before admission. Formal entry uses queued extraction; library builds without a queue retain in-process writeback. A successful answer does not prove extraction/indexing finished. Retrieval may call paid embedding, then chat may call a paid model; SDK retries and later extraction can add invocations. Retrieval errors, including embedding quota denial, degrade to an ungrounded answer; abstained refers to memory retrieval, not a promise the generated answer is empty or unknown. Response contains complete answer and selected citations, no token stream; history_included describes model history. message_id identifies the persisted assistant message, whose stored references contain only version IDs; citation value is required arbitrary JSON including null. Unlike SSE, this legacy JSON route has no generation ID, cancellation receipt, explicit deadline, no-store guarantee or distributed serialization. Concurrent JSON sends may overlap. HTTP disconnect does not establish upstream cancellation. After Evidence admission, chat/config/quota/database/save failures can leave user/file Evidence and queued work without an assistant reply; some409 responses can occur after paid work. The existing error boundary also forwards nonretryable SDK HTTP statuses, including upstream400/401/403/422/429, after Evidence admission. These are not reliable proof of local validation/auth rejection. Upstream4xx detail uses the error message as supplied; only5xx detail is fixed. Other upstream error statuses use the default problem response; Retry-After is conditional (local budget/quota), not guaranteed for provider failures. Repeating the same request creates new Evidence; no idempotency key or automatic retry. Ordinary CORS applies, Origin is not universally rejected.

post.summary: Admit user/file Evidence and stream a persisted answer decision
post.description: Same strict message/attachment rules, sanitization limits and global operator scope as JSON send. Both URL UUIDs normalized to lowercase and conversation project checked before revealing busy state; query ignored, ordinary CORS. Requires DB/master key. Before admission, invalid/foreign/archived/broken-history requests use problem+json. Single-instance coordinator permits one active SSE per conversation, excludes competing mutations and caps active SSE generations at32; not a distributed lock. After atomic Evidence/outbox admission, success200 is a text/event-stream byte stream, never a JSON array; a start event is emitted before model preparation. HTTP200/start do not prove generation success. Each frame is event:<type> plus one JSON data line, separated by an empty line; event name must equal data.type. x-sse-event-schema is this contract's extension describing each parsed data object, not an OpenAPI-standard SSE sequencing guarantee. Exactly one start, zero or more nonempty delta frames, then finish or error if transport remains writable. IDs remain constant: start.conversation_id matches URL, generation_id equals persisted assistant message ID, finish.message_id equals generation_id. Delta concatenation is the visible answer; no reasoning or provider-error payload is emitted. finish complete/interrupted is emitted only after assistant persistence; complete reflects accepted SDK termination, not a guarantee finishReason was stop (length/tool-calls can terminate normally). An error GENERATION_FAILED can accompany a saved failed prefix; PERSISTENCE_FAILED means no successful save acknowledgement. EOF/disconnect without a terminal event is unconfirmed, not successful cancellation. No SSE id/retry or Last-Event-ID replay, no automatic retry/resume. Query embedding and chat may bill; chat stream maxRetries=0, other SDK calls/background extraction have their own retry policies. Retrieval errors may degrade to no-memory. Once started, model/config/quota failures become200+error events, not JSON401/429/503. Evidence/queued work can remain after failure. Prefix is saved as interrupted for explicit cancel, disconnect, deadline or shutdown when persistence succeeds; this does not prove provider billing stopped. Default generation deadline300s starts after admission and covers preparation/streaming, not admission DB waits; 30s backpressure abort and deadline+30s transport guard apply, no all-SQL hard timeout. Bounds: delta<=16384 UTF16 units, each encoded event<=128KiB, visible and text+reasoning budgets2MiB, wire8MiB with terminal headroom. Successful SSE headers no-store and X-Accel-Buffering:no. A saved terminal may still be lost in transport; use scoped cancel/status receipt or read history before deciding a new send. Durable work registration does not mean extraction/indexing completed.

post.summary: Request interruption and read the durable generation decision
post.description: All three UUID paths normalized to lowercase. Same global Bearer and request rate budgets; project+conversation+assistant message must match. Query ignored. Body may be absent or JSON null (both normalized to{}); a provided object must be strictly empty. text/plain is parsed but rejected400; unsupported media415. If matching generation is active in this process, signal abort and wait for its persistence decision, not downstream frame draining. Then query saved assistant state. Response200 may be complete/interrupted/failed; it reports the existing durable decision, not a promise the call changed it to interrupted or stopped provider billing. generation_id=message_id; no answer body or citations. Repeating after completion returns same saved decision without model calls or new rows. Unknown/foreign/non-assistant/legacy assistant with null generation_status gives404; active generation with failed save gives500, subsequent request after release may instead return404. Multi-instance routing may miss another process's active registry; no distributed cancellation or crash-recovery promise. No guaranteed no-store or end-to-end SQL deadline for this legacy cancellation response. Failure/timeout/429 is not a save receipt; do not resend the original chat request automatically.
